summary: The note describes the origins of Grant Park in Atlanta, established in 1883 when engineer and businessman Lemuel P. Grant donated 100 acres to the city. It covers the city's 1890 acquisition of additional land and appointment of its first park commissioner, Sidney Root, and the 1903 hiring of the Olmsted Brothers to plan the park, which originally included Lake Abana for storm-water runoff.
one_line: History of Grant Park in Atlanta, from its 1883 founding on land donated by Lemuel P. Grant to its 1903 Olmsted Brothers plan.
key_facts: Grant Park in Atlanta was established in 1883.
Lemuel P. Grant, a successful engineer and businessman, gave the city of Atlanta 100 acres (40 ha) for the park in 1883.
Lemuel P. Grant's gift was in the newly developed suburb where he lived.
In 1890, the city of Atlanta acquired another 44 acres (18 ha) for Grant Park.
Sidney Root was appointed as the first park commissioner of Grant Park in 1890.
In 1903, the Olmsted Brothers were hired to create a plan for Grant Park.
The Olmsted Brothers were sons of Frederick Law Olmsted.
The original Grant Park included a lake named Lake Abana.
Lake Abana was built to handle storm-water runoff.
